CADMIUM  SULFURATUM.

Sulpldde  of  Cadmium.  Cd  S.

Discovered  in  1817  by  Stromeyer  and  Herrmann  as  a  constant  associate
of  Zincum,  especially  in  the  Silesian  ores.     The  best  solvent  is  nitric  acid.

Recommended  in  1820  by  Graefe  in  eye  diseases  in  the  place  of  Zincum  ;
afterwards  by  Tott  in  1833.  Experiments  by  Schubarth  on  dogs  were  pub-
lished in  HufelancVs  Journal  about  1821.

H.  J.  Burdock  made  an  insignificant  proving  on  himself  in  1827.  The
first  real  proving  was  made  by  Petroz  in  1854  and  published  in  the  May
number  of  Journale  de  la  Soc.  (raZZtcane,  including  cured  symptoms;  it  ap-
peared in  the  Oct.  number  of  the  Allg.  Horn.  Zeitung  and  in  1856  in  HirscheVs
Archiv,  Vol.  II.  These  were  not  followed  by  any  other  reports  until  1878,
when  Dr.  Hardenstein,  of  Vicksburg,  used  the  remedy  successfull}'^  in  one
of  the  most  murderous  epidemics  of  yellow  fever;  the  application  of  the
remedy  proving  him  to  be  a  master  in  prescribing.  Cadmium  is  no  doubt
a  so-called  antipsoric  of  high  rank.
